title: Quel / quelle / quels / quelles
subtitle: Asking which
explanation: Use quel, quelle, quels, and quelles to ask which. The form changes to match the noun it describes.

title: Préférer
subtitle: Saying prefer
explanation: Use préférer to say that someone prefers something. In questions, French can use préfères-tu or préférez-vous.

examples.eng: I like that one but I prefer this one.
examples.fre: J'aime cela mais je préfère ceci.

title: Meilleur / meilleure
subtitle: Saying better
explanation: Use meilleur for masculine nouns and meilleure for feminine nouns when saying better.

examples.eng: The wine is always better here.
examples.fre: Le vin est toujours meilleur ici.

title: Meilleur que
subtitle: Better than
explanation: Use meilleur que or meilleure que to compare two things and say one is better than the other.

examples.eng: The cheese here is better than the cheese there.
examples.fre: Le fromage ici est meilleur que le fromage là.

examples.eng: I think the chicken is better than the turkey.
examples.fre: Pour moi, le poulet est meilleur que la dinde.

examples.eng: That one is better than this one.

title: Ce / cet / cette / ces
subtitle: This and that before nouns
explanation: Use ce, cet, cette, and ces before nouns. Add -ci for this/these and -là for that/those.

title: Ceci and cela
subtitle: This one and that one
explanation: Use ceci for this one and cela for that one when no noun comes after it.

examples.eng: Do you want this or that?
examples.fre: Veux-tu ceci ou cela? / Voulez-vous ceci ou cela?

title: Le meilleur / la meilleure
subtitle: The best
explanation: Use le meilleur or la meilleure to say the best. The form changes with the noun.

title: Plus ... que
subtitle: More than / -er than
explanation: Use plus + adjective + que to say more ... than. This is how French often makes comparisons.

examples.eng: This wine is more delicious than that wine.
examples.fre: Ce vin-ci est plus délicieux que ce vin-là.

examples.eng: Marie is more beautiful than Jeanne.
examples.fre: Marie est plus belle que Jeanne.

examples.eng: Dinner was more delicious than lunch.
examples.fre: Le dîner était plus délicieux que le déjeuner.

title: Moins ... que
subtitle: Less than
explanation: Use moins + adjective + que to say less ... than.

examples.eng: Calais is less expensive than Paris.
examples.fre: Calais est moins cher que Paris.

examples.eng: The car is less quick than the train.
examples.fre: La voiture est moins rapide que le train.

examples.eng: Pierre is less intelligent than Michel.
examples.fre: Pierre est moins intelligent que Michel.

title: Pire
subtitle: Worse
explanation: Use pire to say worse. It is the opposite of meilleur in many comparison sentences.

examples.eng: The wine is always worse here.
examples.fre: Le vin est toujours pire ici.

title: Pire que
subtitle: Worse than
explanation: Use pire que to compare two things and say one is worse than the other.

examples.eng: The cheese here is worse than the cheese there.
examples.fre: Le fromage ici est pire que le fromage là.

examples.eng: I think the chicken is worse than the turkey.
examples.fre: Pour moi, le poulet est pire que la dinde.

examples.eng: That hotel was worse than this hotel.
examples.fre: Cet hôtel-là était pire que cet hôtel-ci.

title: Le pire / la pire
subtitle: The worst
explanation: Use le pire, la pire, or les pires to say the worst.

title: Il fait + weather
subtitle: Talking about weather
explanation: Use il fait with weather adjectives such as beau, chaud, froid, and mauvais.

examples.eng: I hope it's not too cold out today.
examples.fre: J'espère qu'il ne fait pas trop froid aujourd'hui.

title: Il faisait
subtitle: Weather in the past
explanation: Use il faisait to describe weather in the past.

title: Trop
subtitle: Too
explanation: Use trop before an adjective or adverb to say too.

examples.eng: That car is too small for us.
examples.fre: Cette voiture-là est trop petite pour nous.

examples.eng: I think it's too hot today.
examples.fre: Pour moi, il fait trop chaud aujourd'hui.
N'arrive pas / N'arrivez pas trop tôt.

title: Assez
subtitle: Enough / quite
explanation: Use assez to mean enough or quite. It can describe quantity or intensity.

examples.eng: There weren't enough shops to visit.
examples.fre: Il n'y avait pas assez de magasins à visiter.
Je n'avais pas assez de temps.

title: Il y avait
subtitle: There was / there were
explanation: Use il y avait to say there was or there were in the past.

examples.eng: There was a lot to see.
examples.fre: Il y avait beaucoup à voir.

title: Avoir in the imperfect
subtitle: Had / used to have
explanation: Use j'avais, tu avais, il avait, and the other imperfect forms of avoir to say had or used to have.

examples.eng: I used to have a house in France.

title: Avoir faim / froid / chaud
subtitle: Feelings with avoir
explanation: French often uses avoir for feelings where English uses to be, such as I am hungry or I am cold.

title: Avoir raison / avoir tort
subtitle: Being right or wrong
explanation: Use avoir raison for to be right and avoir tort for to be wrong.

examples.fre: Tu as raison. / Vous avez raison.

title: Avoir peur de
subtitle: Being scared of
explanation: Use avoir peur to say someone is scared. Add de before the thing or person they are scared of.

examples.eng: Why was he scared of her?

title: Avoir besoin de
subtitle: Needing something
explanation: Use avoir besoin de before an infinitive or noun to say that someone needs something.

examples.fre: J'ai besoin de manger quelque chose.

title: Avoir envie de
subtitle: Feeling like / fancying
explanation: Use avoir envie de before an infinitive or noun to say someone feels like doing or having something.

examples.fre: J'ai envie de sortir ce soir.

examples.eng: She didn't feel like coming with us.
examples.fre: Elle n'avait pas envie de venir avec nous.

title: Avoir l'intention de
subtitle: Planning to do something
explanation: Use avoir l'intention de before an infinitive to say someone plans or intends to do something.

examples.eng: I had the intention of going with you.
examples.fre: J'avais l'intention d'aller avec toi / vous.

examples.eng: We don't plan on staying here.
examples.fre: Nous n'avons pas l'intention de rester ici.

title: Ne ... pas with avoir
subtitle: Negating avoir
explanation: Put ne before the form of avoir and pas after it to make the sentence negative.

title: Inversion questions
subtitle: Verb before subject
explanation: In formal or practice-style questions, French can put the verb before the subject, joined with a hyphen.

examples.eng: When do they need to leave?

title: Est-ce que questions
subtitle: Simple yes/no questions
explanation: Use est-ce que at the start of a statement to turn it into a yes/no question.

examples.eng: Is it better for you here?
examples.fre: Est-ce que c'est meilleur pour toi / vous ici?

examples.eng: Is this one the best one?
examples.fre: Est-ce que ceci est le meilleur?
Est-ce que c'est meilleur ou pire?

title: De quoi
subtitle: What about / what of
explanation: Use de quoi when the question needs de, such as asking what someone is scared of or what someone needs.

title: De quel / de quelle
subtitle: Which one with de
explanation: Use de quel, de quelle, de quels, or de quelles when asking which noun after de.

examples.fre: De quel vin as-tu / avez-vous envie?

title: Combien de
subtitle: How much / how many
explanation: Use combien de before a noun to ask how much or how many.

examples.eng: How much wine have you drunk?

title: Pour combien de temps
subtitle: For how long
explanation: Use pour combien de temps or pour combien de jours to ask about duration.

title: Puis-je + infinitive
subtitle: May I / can I
explanation: Use puis-je before an infinitive for polite questions like May I go? or Can I open?

examples.eng: Can I have two bags, please?
examples.fre: Puis-je avoir deux sacs, s'il vous plaît?

title: Vouloir + infinitive
subtitle: Wanting to do something
explanation: Use vouloir before another verb in the infinitive to say someone wants to do something.

examples.eng: What do you want to do today?
examples.fre: Que veux-tu faire aujourd'hui? / Que voulez-vous faire aujourd'hui?

examples.eng: Do you want to take that with you?
examples.fre: Veux-tu prendre ça avec toi? / Voulez-vous prendre ça avec vous?

examples.eng: I'm very hungry, I want to eat something.
examples.fre: J'ai très faim, je veux manger quelque chose.

title: Passé composé with avoir
subtitle: Completed past actions
explanation: Many past actions use avoir plus a past participle, such as j'ai essayé or j'ai entendu.

examples.eng: I tried the cake but it wasn't very good.
examples.fre: J'ai essayé le gâteau mais il n'était pas très bon.

examples.eng: I don't know if he heard me.
examples.fre: Je ne sais pas s'il m'a entendu.

title: Direct object pronouns
subtitle: It before the verb
explanation: Short words like le, la, l’, and les can stand for it or them and usually go before the verb.

examples.eng: Do you want to try it?
I was going to try it.

title: Un peu plus / beaucoup plus
subtitle: A bit more / a lot more
explanation: Use un peu plus for a bit more and beaucoup plus for a lot more.

examples.eng: This one is smaller but that one is a lot more expensive.
examples.fre: Ceci est plus petit mais cela est beaucoup plus cher.

examples.eng: I wonder if this is a lot more expensive than that.
examples.fre: Je me demande si ceci est beaucoup plus cher que cela.

title: Quand
subtitle: Saying when
explanation: Use quand to say when. It can introduce a time idea inside a longer sentence.

examples.eng: I prefer when it's warm out.
examples.fre: Je préfère quand il fait chaud.

examples.eng: I don't like eating ice cream when I'm cold.
examples.fre: Je n'aime pas manger de la glace quand j'ai froid.

examples.eng: I was scared when I was in Paris.
examples.fre: J'avais peur quand j'étais à Paris.
